newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat oil firm INA forms new groups to sell.
newsitem.headline: Croat oil firm INA forms new groups to sell.

text.p: Croatia's oil giant INA has formed three new subsidiaries it will offer for sale in line with its plans to get rid of all companies not directly linked
with oil production, the company paper said on Tuesday.

The three, no longer bearing INA prefix, were formed in December, following INA's announcements that it would focus only on oil production and processing in 1997. They should be sold later to help pay out the company's $800 million foreign debts.
CROSCO d.o.o includes technology services firms, HOSTIN d.o.o groups INA's hotels and sports facilities and INFO-centar d.o.o. comprises computer services, the paper said.
The selloff is also meant to cover INA's large public debts now burdening one of Croatia's biggest ailing banks -- Privredna Banka, currently being overhauled.

The paper quoted economy minister Davor Stern as saying clearing INA's portfolio would help it gather fresh funds to modernize its refinery in the Adriatic port of Rijeka. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
